title: Course plan
description: The part of a course that is planned and not yet written: every unit with every module, and what each module teaches. One file per language, content/<lang>/course-plan.json. Nothing here names a language: ids are graph ids, and text in the language being taught sits in a native-language string between braces. Positions, word counts and where each level is reached are computed by plan:check, never stored.

native.description: The language the plan's prose is written in.

levels.description: The unit by whose end each level must be reached. plan:check fails when the course reaches a level later.

words_to_add.description: Words the plan teaches that the graph does not hold yet. Each is taught by the module named. When a word becomes a headword, its entry leaves this list.

held_patterns.description: Patterns whose needs are met that the plan leaves for the level after it, each with the reason. plan:check asks every other ready pattern to be taught.

later.description: Topics kept for the level after this plan.

can_do.description: What the learner can do at the end, observable.

cast.description: Who is in the unit: name, age, who they are to each other, and a lead's look.

situations.description: The real things to get done that the lessons practise.

facts.description: The unit's cast facts, one world for every module: who likes what, who lives where and on which floor, where each place is and when it opens. Every brief of the unit prints them.

culture.description: What the unit carries of the country: its history and its customs.

sound.description: The sounds this unit's words make a good place to practise.

carry.description: Words the unit's practice set and exam must carry, because no later lesson of the unit can use them again.

notes.description: Why the unit is built this way: where its guides sit and why.

open.description: Points to settle when the unit is written.

outline.description: The unit's lines in the course outline (course.json), which plan:stubs writes: its description, a short can-do and a French example. Its can_do comes from the unit's can_do.

module_key.description: Permanent. A module keeps its key when it moves or is retitled.

goal.description: For a lesson, what the learner can do after it. For a guide, what it gathers.

situation.description: The situation the module opens and closes in.

words.description: Every new word, each taught once in the whole course. A reading's are the words of its table.

carrier.description: What carries the module's new words: the pattern or the verb taught first, which every other new word is met through. A list of six or more new words with no new verb, frame word or pattern fails the check.

met_through.description: For each new word, the owned material its first sentence is built on: the carrier, earlier words of this module, or words and patterns taught before. Keys are the module's words.

reuses.description: Words the learner already has that this module's pattern gives a new job.

gathers.description: For a guide: the patterns it gathers into one rule or explains, often for the first time; what it gathers counts as taught from its position.

practises.description: Patterns taught earlier that this module leans on.

minutes.description: First-pass study minutes for one sitting, by the recipe constants. A reading in parts gives the minutes of one part.

culture_note.description: A short note on a custom, where it meets one of the module's words.

spoken.description: The small words of speech, short forms and slang the module's dialogue uses.

summary.description: One line on a practice set.

reading.description: A reading is one module with one word table. A long reading has parts, each read in one sitting.

type.description: The human situation the part is about: an id from the shared catalog, scripts/plan/reading-types.json.

kind.description: story; article on a custom, a piece of history or a place; exposition with no characters or plot; learning-alongside, where a character learns with the reader.

type_note.description: One line on why this reading took its type, when the language's culture fits a different type better than the guide suggests at this point.

id.description: The id the word will take in the graph.

use.description: recognize: the learner must understand it and is never asked to produce it.

held.description: Why the word cannot join the graph yet.
